subject: Mobile invite blocked by embedded WebView — Papertrail onboarding
messages:
From: Ethan Roberts <ethan.roberts@papertrailmfg.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Can't complete supplier invite — mobile app WebView blocks login

Hi Jonas,

We're trying to accept the supplier invite you sent for Papertrail Manufacturing but we keep getting stuck at the final step. Steps we see:
1) Click invite link from email on our Android device (Pixel 7, Android 14)
2) The link opens inside our company app's embedded WebView (we have a procurement portal shortcut inside the app)
3) The “Accept & Continue” button briefly flashes, then the page reloads back to the app frame and we end up on a blank white screen.

We've tested on two devices and the same behavior occurs. If we copy the link and open it in Chrome on the phone it works fine. The problem seems limited to the WebView environment.

Attached a screenshot of the blank state (screenshot-accept-button.png) and a short WebView console dump we captured (mobile-weblog.txt). Can you reissue the invite with any workaround token? Or recommend a short-term approach so our procurement team can finish onboarding and get PO uploads going.

Thanks — we need to turn on PO ingest this week to meet a supplier deadline.

Ethan Roberts
Procurement Lead
Papertrail Manufacturing

Hi Ethan — thanks for the details and the attachments.

Short answer: we can reissue a link that forces an external browser handoff and also provide a one-click desktop invite. For immediate unblock, the easiest options are:
- Open the invite in Chrome (copy/paste) on the phone as you discovered.
- If you have an email client that supports “Open in browser”, use that to launch the link outside the embedded view.

Longer term I have looped in Monica (engineering) and Ben (CS/sales). Monica — can you triage the WebView redirect behavior? The logs indicate a possible redirect being blocked when the accept flow tries to POST to the SSO endpoint inside a non-top-level browsing context.

Ethan — I will also issue a temporary invite variant that appends a direct-login hint parameter (force_external=true) which should force the provider to hand off to an external browser. Before I reissue, can you confirm whether Kate or anyone on the procurement team prefers a desktop link? If we can move PO upload to desktop for the short term, that will be safest for this week's deadline.

I'll follow up with the reissued link and an internal ticket number.

— Jonas Weber

Checklist to triage:
- Reproduce on Android WebView (API level and WebView implementation matters)
- Confirm whether the accept flow uses top-level navigation or a form POST that expects same-origin top context
- Check for presence of X-Frame-Options/CSP or cross-origin navigation protections that kill the redirect inside an embedded context
- Possible quick fixes: append force_external=true to the invite link (client-side hack), server-side option to render a simple landing page with an explicit “Open in browser” CTA, or reissue invite targeted to desktop only.

Logs attached (mobile-weblog.txt). This is time-sensitive — customer timeline: PO ingest by Friday. Can you confirm ETA for a mitigation? If you need infra help I can push an emergency reissue path from my console.

Hi Ethan, Jonas, Ben — quick update after triage:

Root cause summary:
We reproduced the failure in Chromium WebView when a redirect during the accept flow attempts to result in a top-level navigation to the SSO provider while embedded in a non-top-level browsing context. Some host apps (including your procurement app's WebView) set flags that prevent this cross-context navigation; when that happens the client receives a successful accept response but the subsequent navigation is suppressed by the WebView and the page ends up blank. The console dump you provided shows the same navigation being suppressed.

Short-term mitigations (choose one):
1) Reissue an invite with the query param force_external=true — this triggers a one-time landing page that renders an explicit button labeled “Open in external browser”. When tapped this performs window.open to a top-level context and avoids the blocked navigation. I can reissue this immediately.
2) Ask users to long-press the invite link and select “Open in browser” or copy/paste into Chrome (what you already observed).
3) We can generate a desktop-only invite link from our console if you prefer to onboard the procurement admin on a laptop for the PO uploads this week.

Longer-term fix: engineering ticket SUP-4127 is scheduled to add a server-side fallback to detect embedded contexts and render an explicit external browser handoff page automatically for affected clients. Estimated delivery: next sprint (2 weeks).

Action I took: reissued a temporary invite with force_external=true and sent the private accept link directly to Ethan (separate email to avoid spam filters). If you didn't receive it, check spam/promotions.

Ethan — let me know which mitigation you prefer. If you want the immediate reissue to the broader procurement team, confirm the email addresses and I will send the force_external variant to all of them.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Software Engineer, Onboarding Team
Redwood Inference
